title: Press a corn tortilla to 14 cm in a cast-iron tortilla press: ball centred, lever pressed down, press opened again
instruction: Press the masa ball into a corn tortilla at least 14 cm across, then open the press.
context: Pressing corn tortillas in a hand press is an everyday home-cooking job across Mexico and Central America and in many homes and taquerias elsewhere. WebstaurantStore's guide "How to Use a Tortilla Press": "Place a ball of tortilla dough in the center of the press over the paper." "Lower the top plate of your tortilla press onto the dough." "Press down on the handle of the tortilla press." "Lift the top plate" and peel the tortilla off. The hand skill: set a soft 4 cm ball down in the middle of the bottom plate (a few cm off and the tortilla is squeezed out past the plates' edge); lower the 1.2 kg cast-iron top plate onto it by its boss; swing the lever over onto the boss and push its end down firmly, about 20 N through 4 cm; then lift the lever back and open the top plate past upright onto its stop. One arm can do most of it; here one arm works the lever and the other the ball and the top plate.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) 8-inch cast-iron tortilla press (like the Victoria TOR-003, 3.9 kg), fixed on rubber feet: bottom plate 20 cm across, 1.2 cm thick, centred at x 22, y 0, top 3.0 cm up; top plate 20 cm, 1.2 cm thick, 1.2 kg, hinged along x at y 11.5, 3.6 cm up, with a round pressing boss 2.4 cm across and 4 cm long (along x) at its centre, starting swung open 100 deg onto its hinge stop; freezer-bag plastic squares 17 x 17 cm on both plates. (2) Lever, 0.45 kg iron bar 2.2 x 1.4 cm, pivoted along x at y -11.8, 7.4 cm up, 28.8 cm to its end; lying over the press it bears on the boss 11.8 cm from the pivot; it starts swung up 95 deg onto its stop. (3) Corn masa ball, 4 cm, 35 g, loose, on a white plate 11 cm across, 1.2 cm tall, at x 12, y -21. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every control step: the top plate's and the lever's angles, the ball's position, the tortilla's centre and diameter d. 0.25 the masa has been pressed between the plates (the top plate came down onto the ball on the bottom plate); 0.5 d >= 10 cm; 0.75 d >= 14 cm; 1.0 (success, held 1 s) d >= 14 cm and the press open again, lever and top plate both swung back 90 deg or more onto their stops. 0 for the whole run once the tortilla runs past the plates' edge (centre offset plus radius over 10 cm). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the end of the video, and a ruler across the tortilla on the open bottom plate (its smallest width; any masa squeezed past the edge).
reset_notes: Peel off the tortilla, smooth fresh plastic squares onto both plates, swing the top plate and the lever back onto their stops, and put a fresh 35 g masa ball (instant corn masa flour and water, about 1 : 1.2 by weight, kneaded 2 min and rested 10 min covered; a batch keeps a few hours) on the small plate. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The masa is a rule: once the top plate comes down on the ball, it becomes a disc of equal volume (33.5 cm3), centred where the ball lay, that only gets thinner while the plates' force on it exceeds 60 N x 2.18 mm / h (a stiff spring on the top plate's hinge carries it); 60 N on the dough gives 14 cm. These are estimates, not measured on real masa: a real trial measures the real tortilla. The plastic sheets are drawn only; the press is fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the masa ball on its plate and pushed at it again and again without lifting it, knocking the lever over onto the open top plate; the ball never reached the press); demo: 1.0
